summary: Tested the Mess Unit Conversion Engine end to end as admin, in the UI (Playwright) and through the API (pytest, 10 of 11 pass). The acceptance case works: 500 gram at Rs 400/kg shows '= 0.5 kg', line total Rs 200 and grand total Rs 200 in the receipt dialog. The same Rs 200 appears in the receipt list item table, the Pending Approvals modal (approval-items-total), the stored receipt and the posted stock ledger (qty_in 0.5 kg, unit_cost 400, expense Rs 200), and in the GST bill computation (compute_mess_tax). Other cases also work: Rice 2 bag (factor 25) gives '= 50 kg' and Rs 20,000; Bread offers only 'packet' with no converted preview and gives Rs 1,000; Eggs 2 dozen at Rs 6/piece gives '= 24 piece' and Rs 144. Unit dropdowns only offer compatible units. Create Receipt without a bill shows the toast and the dialog stays open; with a bill it saves. Unit Review opens read-only, shows the empty state and changes no data. Item Master saves consumption_unit and allow_decimal. Consumption entered in gram deducts the right base qty (200 -> 199.5 kg). Regression: all 9 Mess tabs load, Monthly Report PDF downloads, existing receipt totals are unchanged, no ChunkLoadError.

minor.issue: consumption_unit is not checked against base_unit. An item with base_unit=kg and consumption_unit=litre is saved with 200. The frontend Consumption Unit dropdown (item-cons-unit) also lists every MESS_UNIT. As a result LineEditor defaults the line unit to 'litre', which is not in the compatible options: the select shows 'kg' but the state holds 'litre', and posting fails with 400 'not compatible'.
allow_decimal is stored but never enforced. 0.5 qty is still accepted for an item with allow_decimal=false, and the frontend inputs do not restrict it either.

Approval recomputes qty_base from the item's CURRENT config (_to_base_qty(it, accepted_qty, unit)) instead of the accepted_qty_base stored on the line. If conversion_factor is edited between creation and approval, the stock-in no longer matches the amount that was approved. Use ln['accepted_qty_base'] when rate_basis=='base'.

Pre-existing: the global mess_items.avg_cost is overwritten with ONE center's avg_cost after every approval. Approving a Rs 400/kg receipt at one center changed the Rice master avg_cost from 55 to 400. Testing agent restored it to 55.324.

ui_bugs.issue: React duplicate key warning: key={s.item_id}, but under 'All authorized' the same item can have a stock row in several centers (Rice now does). Use key={`${s.center_id}-${s.item_id}`}. The same pattern appears at L492, L626, L1548 and L1741.

issues: The Unit column is too narrow. Selected units show cut off as 'gra', 'bag', 'pac', 'doz', so users cannot see which unit they picked. Widen the Unit column (e.g. w-24/w-28) or shrink the Item column.
One center in the receipt-center dropdown has an EMPTY name (id 7f11829a-...). It shows as a blank option and the receipt subtitle shows '—'. This is a data issue.
'Pending with' badge repeats 'Center Manager (initiator) · Center Manager (initiator)' (pre-existing).

action_items: Validate consumption_unit with compatible_units(item) in POST/PUT /mess/items, and limit the item-cons-unit dropdown to compatibleUnits({base_unit, purchase_unit, conversion_factor}).
Enforce allow_decimal (backend 400 when a fractional qty is entered for allow_decimal=false; optionally set step=1 on the inputs).
In _mess_post_receipt, use the stored accepted_qty_base for rate_basis=='base' lines instead of recomputing from the current item config.
Widen the Unit column in the ReceiptDialog so selected units are fully readable.
Fix duplicate React keys in the stock/report tables under multi-center view (key on center_id+item_id).
critical_code_review_comments: The backend engine (unit_conversion.py) and the frontend mirror (lib/units.js) match each other and handle weight, volume, count and packaging-via-conversion_factor correctly.

The unit-review heuristic assumes every legacy line priced in a non-base, non-purchase unit was priced per base. A legacy line genuinely priced per gram would be flagged incorrectly. It is acceptable because the review is read-only.
The frontend clamps taxable at 0 (Math.max) and the backend does not, so a discount larger than the line amount would give different totals in the preview and the saved receipt.
MessManagement.jsx is 1758 lines; consider splitting it (ReceiptDialog, ItemDialog, Tabs).

success_rate.backend: 91% (10/11; the failure is the consumption_unit validation gap)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows pass (minor design/key issues noted)
